spans.s:
Kuñcikā
or kuJjikA name of C. by Kṛṣṇa Mitra, or Durbalācārya son of Rāma Sevaka on Vaiyākaraṇasiddhānta mañjūṣā. Pt.. Chowkh. Skt. Ser. Benares, 1925. [Page174-b]

Kuñcitāṅghristava
hymn in 315 verses on Naṭarāja an. His famous shrine a. Chidambaram an. the myths an. esoteric significance of the same. by Umāpati, Śivācārya of Chidambaram. Current with the Dīkṣitas, priests an. custodians of the temple an. ptd. by them with Tamil meaning a. Chidambaram, 1958.

Kuñcu_nampūtirippāṭ
alias Śāstṛśarman of Māntiṭṭa house in Kerala; modern writer.
--Gaṅgālaharī in 24 Taraṅgas. Pt.. 1957.

Kuñja
poet. Skm. p. 119. C.. Kuñjarāja below.

Kuñjakambalatantra
one of the 64 tantras mentioned in Śivatattvaratnākara, p. 4, Madras edn. 1927.

Kuñjavihāra_kavicandra
younger brother of Rāmacandra of Hārīta gotra.
--Vrajakautukāmṛta, a kāvya on Kṛṣṇa's boyhood.

Kuñjavihāryaṣṭaka
stotra vallabhīya. Pt.. with Vedāntakāmadhenu by

Kuñjavihāryaṣṭaka
stotra on Kṛṣṇa. AS. p. 302. C.. the one by Rūpa given below.

Kuñjavihāryaṣṭaka
stotra on Kṛṣṇa. Caitanya school. (beg. indranIlamaNimaJjulavarNa).

Kuñjavihāryaṣṭaka
on Kṛṣṇa, in 9 verses. (beg. avirataratibandhuH smeratAbandhurazrIH). by Rūpa Gosvāmin. RASB.

Kuñjikāstotra
in 13 verses from Ḍāmaratantra.
Pt.. Br. St. Ratnākara. Pt. I. p.. 375-76. N. S. Press, 1952. [Page175-a.

Kuññikuṭṭan_tampurān
alias Rāmavarma of Cranganore Palace, Kerala (1865-1913 A. D.).
--Āryāśataka.
--Kirātarudrastava.
--Kirātārjunīyavyāyoga.
--Kṛtajñasturuṣkah2.
--Guruvāyupureśabhujangastotra.
Pt.. Kottakkal 1911.
--Jarāsandhavadha.
--Daśakumāracarita.
--Babhruvāhanavijaya.
--Vilambimañjūṣā.
--Śaṅkaragurucarita.
--Subhadrāharaṇa.
--Svayaṁvaramantrākṣaramālā.
Some of these, ptd. in Malayalam script in his collected works, Kottakkal, 1922. See Contribution of Kerala to Skt. Lit. p. 250.

Kuññuṇṇi_kurup
of Kunniyūr house a. Kuṭṭamat in Kasargode (Kerala), son of Śaṅkaravarma Rāja of Kaṭattanād an. Śrīdevī Keṭṭilamma. (1813-1885 A. D.).
--Kapotasandeśa.
--Devīmāhātmya in 130 verses.
--Vyāsotpattisaṁkṣepa.
See Contribution of Kerala to Skt. Lit. p. 269.

Kuññuṇṇi_nampiyār
alias Jayanta of Paṭṭat family in Irinjalakkuḍa, Kerala (1804-1874); patronised by Svāti Tirunāl Rāmavarma, King of Travancore.
--Rasaratnākara bhāṇa.
